messages:
tanya.r: Quick RFC follow-up: propose extracting a tiny policy gateway that returns per-route decisions so routers stay lock-free.
mike.h: yes please. router latency regressions are real when policy logic blocks.
lee: contract idea: sync call returns {action, target_variant, ttl_s, code, meta}. Router caches and enforces.
oncall-bot: incident-note: recent rollout saw 3x p99 spike in us-west at 5402000000.
mike.h: failure modes to handle: infra (latency/errors), correctness (eval regressions), and cost (unexpected token spikes).
tanya.r: agree. different cooldowns per class. for correctness require human-reviewed canary + eval pass before auto-rollback.
lee: region-local decisions by default. KV with region affinity, global override for org incidents. avoids cross-region chattiness.
mike.h: TTL/backoff pattern: initial 60s, exponential backoff on repeated triggers, cap 1h. include stability_window before unwinding.
tanya.r: add risk_tier label on requests (interactive|batch|background). policy can choose to divert only low-risk traffic.
lee: hedging should be opt-in per-route and budgeted. hedging reduces tails but can double cost.
mike.h: prefer enumerated reason codes (LATENCY_P99, OOM, EVAL_REGRESSION) not free text for automation.
tanya.r: telemetry: attach decision_trace id to request logs and persist inputs + outputs for 7d for postmortems.
lee: implement minimal DSL for rules, small expression language, policy-as-code in repo with CI simulator to dry-run policies against historical signals.
oncall-bot: deploy-bot: policy-gateway v0.1 staged by @tanya.r at 5402109888 :rocket:
mike.h: action items: tanya write DSL primer + enums, lee draft decision schema + KV semantics, i'll prototype TTL/backoff defaults and escape API.
tanya.r: let's reconvene Thurs. short thread but aligned.
